articles.title: Google AIサブスクに「Colab」有料特典をバンドル　「高性能GPU」にアクセス可能に
articles.topic: Google Colab / Google AI Subscription / GPU / Background Execution
facts: Google AI subscribers are being given premium Colab benefits including priority access to faster accelerators and more powerful machines.
Google AI Ultra adds uninterrupted background execution and Premium GPU access so long-running training jobs can continue without keeping a browser tab open.
Existing Colab subscriptions are unchanged and Google says the benefits can be stacked with Google AI subscription benefits.
The new benefits are rolling out over the next few weeks in Colab-supported countries.
articles.boundary: This is a subscription entitlement and priority-access change, not a guarantee of unlimited accelerator capacity. Uninterrupted background execution and Premium GPU access are specifically described for Google AI Ultra, and rollout is gradual.

articles.title: YouTube、クリエイター向け新機能を多数発表　Geminiによる会話型編集、動画のA/Bテスト、ライブ配信者のマッチングなど
articles.topic: YouTube / Gemini / Conversational Editing / A/B Testing / Creator Tools
facts: YouTube announced a Gemini-powered conversational editing assistant for Shorts and YouTube Create that can draft an initial edit and then suggest reordering, trimming and beat synchronization through chat.
Creators can move back and forth between the conversational assistant and manual timeline editing.
YouTube says a forthcoming video A/B test can compare up to three edited versions, extending its earlier title and thumbnail testing.
YouTube also announced AI comment moderation, creator-live matching and other creator tools, but timing and regional availability were not specified for most functions.
articles.boundary: Most features were announced rather than universally released, and timing/region are unspecified for many of them. YouTube's usage and commerce figures are vendor-reported adoption metrics, not independent outcome measurements.

articles.title: 「ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ万能説」崩壊　AIエージェント時代に企業が迫られる“防御の再設計”
articles.topic: AI Agent Security / JIT Privilege / Least Privilege / Human in the Loop / Dynamic Policy
facts: The article argues that agent authorization needs semantic and task-level context rather than relying only on department, title or static metadata.
It recommends just-in-time and short-lived least privilege so agents receive only the permissions needed for the current task rather than broad standing access.
The article describes a flight-plan style model in which allowed behavior is pre-defined and automation stops when behavior deviates from that plan.
Human approval is treated as one control rather than a universal safety boundary because machine-speed actions can outpace manual review and repeated prompts can create approval fatigue.
articles.boundary: This is an analytical Japanese article synthesizing external guidance and threat examples. Claims about specific external incidents or NIST guidance remain attributed secondary-source claims here unless separately reproduced from their originals; the implementation advice is not a claim that HITL is never useful.

articles.title: 開発者の84％が「AIコーディングによる生産性向上」を実感――だがその効果をどう測定？
articles.topic: AI Coding / Engineering Productivity / Agent Adoption / Measurement / DORA
facts: GitKraken surveyed 554 developers and engineering leaders in its customer and user community during 2026.
The report says 96.4% of teams have adopted AI coding tools, 84% of developers feel more productive and 43% say they feel much more productive.
Only 20% are described as able to measure AI productivity impact; 39% of organizations have no measurement method and another 33% rely on developer self-report.
The report recommends establishing delivery and quality baselines and measuring agents on cost, cycle time, review burden and shipped-output quality rather than relying only on perceived speed.
articles.boundary: This is a vendor/community survey and the productivity result is self-reported, not a randomized causal measurement. GitKraken states that its audience skews toward developers already engaged with modern Git and engineering tooling, and some subgroups should be read directionally.

articles.title: “作成者しか分からないExcelマクロ”の仕様解読、AIで「3日→30分」に　IT企業はどう実現？
articles.topic: IBM Bob / Legacy Modernization / Excel VBA / Code Comprehension / Web Migration
facts: NICP used IBM Bob to analyze a legacy Excel/VBA quotation macro and generate documentation describing code structure, processing and data structures.
NICP and IBM report that understanding the macro specification fell from an average of one to three days to about 30 minutes in this case.
A broader migration that staff had estimated at roughly six weeks was completed in about 2.5 days in the reported project, with staff reviewing and testing generated work.
The resulting logic was rebuilt as a web application and the organization says data can now be accumulated, searched and reused.
articles.boundary: This is one company case reported by NICP and IBM, not a controlled benchmark. The one-to-three-day and six-week baselines include internal estimates, human review and testing remained necessary, and the result should not be generalized to arbitrary legacy systems.
